TITLE: What's in your food?

[reading 40] What's in your food? · 1–6

## 1 Answer the questions.
FROM: speaking
HELP: Matnni o'qishdan oldin o'ylab ko'ring va inglizcha qisqa yozing. Bu yerda xato javob yo'q.
> What do you think the ingredients are in a chicken burger?
> What do you think the ingredients are in a strawberry milkshake?

## 2 Read the article and check your answers in 1.
HELP: Maqolani to'liq o'qing. Keyin burger va kokteylda nimalar borligini tanlang.
TEXT: What's in your food?
"""
It's lunch time. You're hungry so you buy yourself a chicken burger and a strawberry milkshake. Yum! But have you got any idea what exactly is inside the food you're eating?

Of course, in the chicken burger there's some chicken. There's also some tomato and some cheese, and there's even some healthy salad with it. But there are also some extra ingredients in the chicken. For example there are at least seven or eight chemical __additives__. They include salt and sugar, to give extra __flavour__ to the meat. But they also include __preservatives__ (to stop the food going bad) and antioxidants (to protect the food from oxygen in the air). The people who make burgers can also __choose__ to add chemical flavours – there are over 4,500 different possibilities! And before they cook the chicken, some already contain chemical __hormones__. These hormones help to make the chickens get big quickly. And, finally, don't forget water! Chicken burgers are 45% water. They add extra water to make the chicken look big.

So, now you're thirsty. It's time to drink some strawberry milkshake. But what's inside that? It's just strawberries and milk, right? Wrong. There's some milk and sugar, but there aren't usually any real strawberries in strawberry milkshakes. Strawberries are expensive and they go bad. Also, modern __consumers__ find that the flavour of real strawberries isn't very strong or very sweet. The solution: scientists create special flavours in laboratories and then they add their secret ingredients. That means that in the end a typical strawberry milkshake can contain 60 chemicals and not one real strawberry. You've got E129, cinnamyl valerate, benzyl isobutyrate, amyl valerate … Mmmm, delicious!

So, as you can see, a simple snack isn't that simple. That explains why we all typically __consume__ between five and seven kilos of food additives a year! Our advice? See if there's a list of ingredients and look at it carefully before you start eating!
"""
? 1 Which of these are in a chicken burger? Choose all. | chicken* | tomato* | cheese* | salad* | salt* | sugar* | water* | strawberries
? 2 Which of these are usually in a strawberry milkshake? Choose all. | milk* | sugar* | real strawberries | chemicals*

## 3 Read the article again. Are these sentences True (T) or False (F)?
SEE: 2
? 1 Chicken burgers and milkshakes have got very simple ingredients. | T | F*
? 2 There is no chicken in a chicken burger. | T | F*
? 3 Antioxidants stop food from going bad because of the air. | T | F*
? 4 Burger companies use a total of 4,500 extra ingredients in each burger. | T | F*
? 5 They don't use strawberries in strawberry milkshakes. | T* | F
? 6 There is just one problem with real strawberries – they cost a lot of money. | T | F*
? 7 The chemicals that scientists create are very important for making milkshakes. | T* | F

## 4 Critical thinking. What does the writer do to make us agree with their ideas? Tick (✓) the ideas below and find examples of them in the text.
SEE: 2
HELP: Muallif qaysi usullardan foydalangan? Bir nechtasini tanlang, keyin matndan bitta misol yozing.
? 1 Tick the ideas. | a They give us facts and figures.* | b They tell us how they feel. | c They give us surprising information.* | d They ask us questions.*
> 2 Write one example from the text for one of your ticks.

## 5 What do the underlined words mean? Guess and then check in your dictionary.
SEE: 2
HELP: Matnda tagiga chizilgan so'zlarni toping. Ma'nosini gapdan taxmin qiling.
? 1 additives | things that people add to food* | things that grow on trees | kinds of meat
? 2 flavour | the colour of food | the taste of food* | the price of food
? 3 preservatives | chemicals that stop food going bad* | people who sell food | healthy vegetables
? 4 choose | decide which one you want* | cook | throw away
? 5 hormones | chemicals in a body that make it change or grow* | small bottles | kinds of salad
? 6 consumers | people who buy and use things* | people who make burgers | scientists
? 7 consume | sell | eat or use* | lose

TITLE: Grammar in context: countable, uncountable, some/any/a/an

[grammar 25] Countable and uncountable · some/any/a/an · 1a–5

## 1a Read the sentences. In a, the words in bold are countable nouns. In b, the words in bold are uncountable.
TEXT: Sentences
"""
a You've got a **burger** and a **milkshake**.
b There's **milk** and **sugar**.
"""
? 1 Countable nouns … | have got a singular and a plural form: a burger, two burgers* | have got only one form: milk, sugar
? 2 Uncountable nouns … | have got a plural form | don't usually have got a plural form*

## 1b Which list below is of countable nouns? Which list is of uncountable nouns?
? 1 LIST A: milk, salt, cheese, juice | countable | uncountable*
? 2 LIST B: apple, banana, egg, strawberry | countable* | uncountable

## 2 Put these food and drink words in the correct column.
HELP: Sanaladigan (countable) yoki sanalmaydigan (uncountable) ekanini tanlang.
EXAMPLE: biscuit → Countable
SORT Countable: biscuit | burger | egg | tomato
SORT Uncountable: bread | butter | cheese | meat | rice | sugar

## 3 Read the sentences. Then match the sentence halves to make rules.
TEXT: Sentences
"""
a You buy **a** chicken burger.
b There aren't **any** strawberries.
c There's **some** cheese.
d Is there **any** milk?
e There are **some** extra ingredients.
f Do you want **an** apple?
g There isn't **any** milk.
h She hasn't got **a** banana.
"""
= 1 We use a/an with => singular countable nouns (apple, banana) in affirmative and negative sentences and questions.
= 2 We use some with => uncountable nouns (water) and plural countable nouns (apples) in affirmative sentences.
= 3 We use any with => uncountable nouns (water) and plural countable nouns (apples) in negative sentences and questions.

## 4 Read about the kitchen and complete the sentences with some, any, a/an.
FROM: photo
TEXT: Tom's kitchen
"""
Look at Tom's kitchen. On the table there are some tomatoes and some strawberries. Next to them there's a big bottle of milk. There's nothing else in the kitchen.
"""
_ 1 He's got [some] tomatoes.
_ 2 He hasn't got [an] egg.
_ 3 He hasn't got [any] apples.
_ 4 He's got [some] strawberries.
_ 5 He hasn't got [any] bread.
_ 6 He's got [some] milk.
_ 7 He hasn't got [a] burger.

## 5 Complete the dialogue with some, any, a/an.
_ Katy: Excuse me, have you got [any] small pizzas with tomatoes?
_ Waitress: No, sorry. We haven't got [any] small pizzas. But we've got [a] big pizza with tomatoes.
_ Katy: Has the pizza got [any] cheese on it?
| Waitress: Yes, it has.
_ Katy: OK. What about drinks? Have you got [any] orange juice?
_ Waitress: Yes, and we've got [some] apple juice too.
| Katy: OK. I'll take the pizza and the apple juice, please!

[lifeskills 25] Planning a balanced diet · 1–3

## Life skills objectives and key concepts.
TEXT: Planning a balanced diet
"""
# Life skills objectives
- To learn about balanced diets
- To assess your own diet
- To plan a balanced diet for the weekend
# Key concepts
- **carbohydrate** (n): Carbohydrates come from pasta, rice and cereals and they give us energy.
- **protein** (n): Proteins come from meat and fish and build and repair muscles, skin, and hair.
- **fat** (n): Fats come from milk, meat and oil and give energy and insulation, but they are unhealthy in large quantities.
- **balanced** (adj): A balanced diet contains a good mixture of all the different food groups.
"""

## 1 The eatwell plate has five coloured sections: two sections of 33%, one of 15%, one of 12% and one of 7%. Match each food group to its section. How many different types of food and drink can you name for each group?
FROM: photo
HELP: Har bir oziq-ovqat guruhi likopchaning qancha qismini egallashini taxmin qiling. Keyingi mashqda matndan tekshirasiz.
? 1 bread, rice, potatoes, pasta | 33%* | 15% | 12% | 7%
? 2 fruit and vegetables | 33%* | 15% | 12% | 7%
? 3 foods and drinks high in fat and/or sugar | 33% | 15% | 12% | 7%*
? 4 meat, fish, eggs, beans | 33% | 15%* | 12% | 7%
? 5 milk and dairy foods | 33% | 15% | 12%* | 7%
> 6 Write all the food and drink words you know for one of the groups.

## 2 Read the text and check your answers in 1.
HELP: Matnni o'qing va 1-mashqdagi javoblaringizni tekshiring.
CHART: Fruit and vegetables 33 #3FAE49 | Bread, rice, potatoes, pasta 33 #F5B700 | Meat, fish, eggs, beans 15 #E8337E | Milk and dairy foods 12 #4FA3F7 | Food and drinks high in fat and/or sugar 7 #B07CFF
TEXT: The eatwell plate
"""
The eatwell plate makes healthy eating easy to understand by showing the types and quantities of foods we need to have a healthy and well-balanced diet. It shows how much of what you eat should come from each group.
# You should try to eat:
# Plenty of fruit and vegetables
Fruit and vegetables give us vitamins, fibre and energy. Most people know that they need to eat five portions of fruit and veg every day, but they don't usually do it. Fruit and veg should be about 33% of what we eat in a day.
# Plenty of bread, rice, potatoes and pasta
These foods give us fibre and energy. Like fruit and vegetables, they should be about a third of what we eat in a day. Some people worry about eating carbohydrates because they think they make you fat. But these foods give us important nutrients, and low carbohydrate diets often have a lot of fat.
# Some milk and dairy products
Milk, cheese and yoghurt are very important because they give us protein, vitamins and calcium. The only problem is that they can contain a lot of fat and this can be bad for our hearts. So either control how much you eat or choose products with low fat, like skimmed or semi-skimmed milk.
# Some meat, fish, eggs and beans
These are a good source of proteins, vitamins and minerals. Meat also contains fat, so try to eat meat with only very little fat and prepare it without much oil. Fish contains very important proteins, and oily fish contains omega 3 fatty acids. Omega 3 is good for your heart.
# Just a small amount of food and drinks high in fat and/or sugar
Fat and sugar give us energy. But eating a lot of fat and sugar makes us have more energy than we need or can use. Look for low fat alternatives instead and try to eat fatty foods only occasionally. Limit cakes, sweets, biscuits and fizzy drinks that contain a lot of sugar.

So, remember to use the eatwell plate. You don't need to get the balance right at every meal. But try to get it right for a whole day or week. And try to choose options that are low in fat, salt and sugar when you can.
"""
? 1 Fruit and vegetables should be about a third of what we eat in a day. | T* | F
? 2 Low carbohydrate diets often have a lot of fat. | T* | F
? 3 You need to get the balance right at every meal. | T | F*

## 3 Read the text again and make notes about each food group. Answer these questions: 1 Why is it good for you? 2 Are there any possible problems?
SEE: 2
HELP: Har bir guruh uchun qisqa yozing: nega foydali va qanday muammosi bor.
> Fruit and vegetables – why good? Any problems?
> Bread, rice, potatoes and pasta – why good? Any problems?
> Milk and dairy products – why good? Any problems?
> Meat, fish, eggs and beans – why good? Any problems?
> Food and drinks high in fat and/or sugar – why good? Any problems?

"""

Kieran: I haven't got much time in the morning, so my snack is a bowl of cereal at eleven o'clock. Or, if I'm out, a cereal bar.

FROM: listening
TEXT: My favourite snack – part 2
"""
Amelia: I think my snack is very healthy. Fruit has got a lot of vitamins and fibre. A milkshake isn't so good – there's a lot of sugar in it – but I only have one when it's really hot.
Kieran: My snack is quite healthy. Cereal gives you a lot of energy, but some cereal bars have got a lot of sugar in them. I should look at the list of ingredients.
Molly: Mine is very healthy. Natural yoghurt has got protein and calcium, and there isn't any sugar in it.

## 7b Do you agree with the four teenagers? Discuss your answers.
FROM: speaking
HELP: To'rt o'smirning fikriga qo'shilasizmi? Ikki gap yozing.
KIND: sentences

"""

He said there is too much sugar in these drinks and a lot of people in the city are getting fat. What do you think? Our first caller is Claire.
Claire: Hi. I think the mayor is right. A supersize drink has got about twenty-five spoons of sugar in it! Some people can't control themselves. When there's a big drink in front of them, they drink it all. They need help, and this law helps them.

Jack: I don't agree with the mayor at all. We aren't children. The government shouldn't tell us what to drink. People should make their own decisions and accept responsibility for them.

Sam: I don't like the law either. Stopping big drinks doesn't help. The important thing is information. Cafés should show how much sugar there is in every drink. Then people can choose.
Presenter: And finally, Natalie.
Natalie: I agree with the mayor, but there's a bigger problem. In a lot of cinemas you can only buy fizzy drinks. They should sell different types of drinks, like water and fruit juice, so people have got a healthy choice.
Presenter: Thank you all. That's all we've got time for today.
"""

[grammar 22] a lot of / much / many · 1–4b

## 1 Read the sentences and then decide if the statements below are true or false.
TEXT: Sentences
"""
a How **much** coffee do they drink a day?
b How **many** people drink coffee every day?

d Is there **a lot of** sugar in fizzy drinks?
e There isn't **much** sugar in this coffee.
f I don't drink **many** fizzy drinks.
"""
? 1 We use much for uncountable nouns and many for countable nouns. | True* | False
? 2 We usually use much and many in questions and negative sentences. | True* | False
? 3 We use a lot of for countable and uncountable nouns. | True* | False
? 4 We use a lot of in affirmative and negative sentences and in questions. | True* | False

TYPE: classwork
LEVEL: A2
BOOK: Gateway A2
UNIT: 6
PAGE: 88–89
LESSON: 8
TITLE: Language checkpoint: Unit 6

[review 40] Grammar reference and revision

## Grammar reference.
TEXT: Grammar reference
"""
# Countable and uncountable nouns
- We can count apples, bananas, eggs, burgers, chips and so there is a singular and a plural form. They are **countable** nouns.
- We cannot count some things and so we do not usually use a plural form. For example, milk, water, bread, salt, cheese. They are **uncountable** nouns.
# some, any, a/an
- We use **some** with uncountable nouns and with plural countable nouns, in affirmative sentences. We've got some water. I've got some apples.
- We use **any** with uncountable nouns and with plural countable nouns, in negative sentences and questions. I haven't got any milk. He hasn't got any apples. Have you got any orange juice? Are there any bananas?
- We use **a/an** with singular countable nouns in affirmative and negative sentences and in questions. **An** goes before a vowel sound. I haven't got a burger. He's got an egg. Have you got an MP3 player?
# a lot of, much, many
- We use **much**, **many**, **a lot (of)** to talk about big quantities.
- We often use **much** in negative sentences and questions, with uncountable nouns. I haven't got much lemonade. Have you got much water?
- We often use **many** in negative sentences and questions, with plural countable nouns. I haven't got many chips. Have you got many eggs?
- We use **a lot of** in affirmative and negative sentences and in questions, with countable and uncountable nouns. I've got a lot of apples. I haven't got a lot of tomatoes. Have you got a lot of water?
- We use **of** when **a lot** comes before a noun. But when there is no noun after **a lot** we do not use **of**. I've got a lot of bananas. Are there any bananas? Yes, there are a lot.
# should/shouldn't
Affirmative | You should eat fruit and vegetables.
Negative | You shouldn't eat a lot of cakes and chocolate.
Question | Should I eat fish?
Short answers | Yes, you should. / No, you shouldn't.
- We use **should** to talk about things that it is a good idea to do. You should drink milk because it's good for you.
- We use **shouldn't** to talk about things that it is not a good idea to do. You shouldn't eat a lot of sugar because it's bad for your teeth.
# Vocabulary
- **Food and drink:** apple · banana · beans · biscuit · bread · burger · butter · cake · cheese · chicken · chips · coffee · soft drink/fizzy drink · egg · fish · grape · ice cream · lemon · lemonade · meat · melon · milk · milkshake · nuts · orange juice · pizza · rice · salad · salt · strawberry · sugar · tea · tomato · water · yoghurt
- **Containers:** bottle · can · carton · cup · glass · packet · slice
"""

## 1 Grammar revision. Are these words countable (C) or uncountable (U)?
? 1 bread | C | U*
? 2 salt | C | U*
? 3 sugar | C | U*
? 4 biscuit | C* | U
? 5 rice | C | U*
? 6 cheese | C | U*
? 7 burger | C* | U
? 8 milk | C | U*

## 2 Read about the picture. Complete the sentences with is, isn't, are, aren't and some, any, a/an.
FROM: photo
TEXT: The picture
"""
On the table there's a loaf of bread, a jug of milk and some red apples. That's all. There's nothing else on the table.
"""
_ 1 There [is some/'s some] bread.
_ 2 There [aren't any/are not any] bananas.
_ 3 There [isn't an/is not an] egg.
_ 4 There [are some] apples.
_ 5 There [isn't any/is not any] water.
_ 6 There [is some/'s some] milk.

## 3 Choose the correct alternative. If both alternatives are correct, choose both.
ANSWER: many
? 1 There are ___ biscuits in the packet. | a lot of* | much
? 2 There isn't ___ milk in the fridge. | much* | many
? 3 Is there ___ water in the bottle? | a lot of* | much*
? 4 Have you got ___ tomatoes? | many* | much
? 5 There's ___ rice. | a lot of* | many

## 4 Write complete sentences giving good advice. Use should or shouldn't.
HELP: Butun gapni yozing: should yoki shouldn't qo'shing.
_ 1 You/write carefully in exams. → [You should write carefully in exams.]
_ 2 Young children/watch very violent films. → [Young children shouldn't watch very violent films.]
_ 3 You/look before you cross the road. → [You should look before you cross the road.]
_ 4 People/help their friends. → [People should help their friends.]
_ 5 You/talk when the teacher is talking. → [You shouldn't talk when the teacher is talking.]
_ 6 Everyone/eat a balanced diet. → [Everyone should eat a balanced diet.]
_ 7 You/speak on your mobile phone in the cinema. → [You shouldn't speak on your mobile phone in the cinema.]

[review 5] Vocabulary revision

CHOOSE: bread | chips | eggs | ice cream | juice | meat | milk | tomatoes
_ 1 We get [milk] from cows.
_ 2 You make [chips] from potatoes.
_ 3 You need [meat/bread] to make a burger.
_ 4 You can make [juice] from oranges.
_ 5 Chickens give us [eggs].

## 3 Containers. Read the descriptions and name the food and drinks and their containers.
FROM: photo

_ b (you can see through it; the drink has no colour) a [glass] of [water]
_ c (a long paper bag of small, sweet, dry cakes) a [packet] of [biscuits]
_ d (small and hot, with a handle; a black drink) a [cup] of [coffee/tea]
_ e (a box made of thick paper, with a straw) a [carton] of [juice/orange juice/apple juice]
_ f (small, red and made of metal) a [can] of [fizzy drink/soft drink/cola/lemonade]

[exam 25] Reading · Listening

## Tip for reading exams.
TEXT: Tip for reading exams
"""
In matching activities, remember …
First, read all parts of the text. Then, read the pieces of information you need to find. Try to find the places in the text where the information is. Read them again slowly.
"""

## 1 Look at the two people in the photos. Do you know who they are? What do you think they have in common? Make a list of ideas.
FROM: photo
TEXT: The photos
"""
Photo 1: Oprah Winfrey, a famous American TV presenter.
Photo 2: Angelina Jolie, a famous American actress.
"""
> What do you think they have in common? Make a list of ideas.

## 2 Read the text. Does it talk about any of your ideas in 1?
TEXT: Rich, famous and generous
"""
They're rich and famous. Oprah Winfrey and Angelina Jolie also give money to help others.

Oprah Winfrey is one of the most famous TV presenters in the world. She was also an actress in the film The Colour Purple. Now, she's an important and successful businesswoman too. She became the first ever African-American billionaire. But her life as a child was difficult and she knew all about being poor. Perhaps that's why she helps people with her money. For example, she gave money to help the victims of Hurricane Katrina in New Orleans and she went there to help them in person. In 2007, she began a school in South Africa to help poor girls to get a good education. She even has her own charity organisation, Oprah's Angel Network.

Angelina Jolie is one of the most famous actresses in the world and she uses her money and fame to help other people. For example, she does a lot of work for an organisation called UNHCR. This organisation helps refugees – people who have to leave their homes and live in camps. She often visits these places to help the people there. But she uses her own money to pay for her trips and she doesn't sleep in five-star hotels. She works and lives in the same conditions as the people who work for UNHCR. In 2012, the UNHCR named her Special Envoy because of all the good work she did. She was the first person to ever take this job. Angelina helps other charities too, such as the Malala Fund. This was started by a fifteen-year-old girl called Malala Yousafzai. It helps young girls in Afghanistan and Pakistan go to school instead of work. Thanks to all her charity work, Jolie was the first person to win the Citizen of the World award.
"""
ANSWER: free
? 1 Does the text talk about any of your ideas? | Yes, a lot of them | Some of them | No, none of them

## 3 Read the text again. Are the sentences about Oprah Winfrey (OW), Angelina Jolie (AJ), or both (B)?
SEE: 2
HELP: Har bir gap kim haqida: Oprah (OW), Angelina (AJ) yoki ikkalasi (B)?
? 1 She received an award for her charity work. | OW | AJ* | B
? 2 She started her own organisation to help others. | OW* | AJ | B
? 3 She does two or three different jobs. | OW | AJ | B*
? 4 She visits people who need help. | OW | AJ | B*
? 5 She had problems when she was young. | OW* | AJ | B
? 6 She doesn't want special conditions when she goes to help other people. | OW | AJ* | B
? 7 She went from having no money to having a lot of money. | OW* | AJ | B

## 5 Read a TV quiz and complete the notes.
FROM: listening
HELP: Viktorinani o'qing va eslatmalarni to'ldiring. So'zlarni to'g'ri yozing: imlo muhim.
TEXT: TV quiz: Who knows?
"""
Host: Welcome to Who Knows? Tonight's subject is Walt Disney. Are you ready, Tom? First question: which famous character did Walt Disney create in 1934?
Tom: Mickey Mouse?
Host: No, sorry. Mickey was in 1928. In 1934 it was Donald Duck.
Tom: Oh, of course!
Host: What did Walt Disney study after school?
Tom: Art. He went to an art school in Chicago.
Host: Correct. Which film did he make in 1940? It has got a lot of classical music in it.
Tom: That's Fantasia.
Host: Yes! How many Oscars did Walt Disney win?
Tom: Twelve?
Host: No. He won twenty-two Oscars. Nobody has won more. It's a record!
Host: Where did he build the original Disneyland?
Tom: In Florida.
Host: No, that's Disney World. The first Disneyland was in California, in 1955.
Host: How old was he when he died?
Tom: He was sixty-five.
Host: Right. And Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs?
Tom: Snow White was the first ever full-length cartoon film.
Host: Correct. Last question: how many fingers did Mickey Mouse have?
Tom: Three fingers and a thumb on each hand!
"""
_ a Walt Disney created the famous character [Donald Duck] in 1934.
_ b After school, Walt Disney studied [art].
_ c Walt Disney made the film Fantasia in [1940].
_ d Walt Disney won [22 Oscars/twenty-two Oscars/22/twenty-two] – a record!
_ e Walt Disney built the original Disneyland in [California].
_ f He was [65/sixty-five] years old when he died.
_ g Walt Disney's Snow White was the first ever [full-length cartoon film/full-length cartoon/cartoon film].
_ h Mickey Mouse had [three fingers/3 fingers] and a thumb on each hand!

## 6 What does Helen say to Daniel? Complete the dialogue with sentences A–H. There are two extra sentences.
HELP: Avval butun suhbatni o'qing. Keyin har bir bo'sh joyga mos gapni tanlang. Ikki gap ortiqcha.
CHOOSE: A Why don't we go there next year with two or three of our friends? | B No, my dad hates flying. | C I know. I love staying in campsites. | D We can stay on campsites. | E No, we didn't eat paella. | F Mostly sightseeing because there are some beautiful cities there. And we went to lots of cafés and restaurants. | G My family and I went to the south of Spain. | H You should. There are a lot of things to see and do.
| Daniel: Where did you go for your holidays last year?
!_ Helen: 1 [G My family and I went to the south of Spain.]
| Daniel: Did you go by plane?
_ Helen: 2 [B No, my dad hates flying.]
| Daniel: What did you do when you got there?
_ Helen: 3 [F Mostly sightseeing because there are some beautiful cities there. And we went to lots of cafés and restaurants.]
| Daniel: Spanish food is great. I'd love to go one day!
_ Helen: 4 [H You should. There are a lot of things to see and do.]
| Daniel: I also want to go to Italy one year.
_ Helen: 5 [A Why don't we go there next year with two or three of our friends?]
| Daniel: That's a good idea. My older brother went last year and he had a great time.
_ Helen: 6 [D We can stay on campsites.]
| Daniel: Yes, hotels are very expensive. But first we have to speak to our parents!

## Tip for writing exams.
TEXT: Tip for writing exams
"""
In writing exams, remember …
When you write to a friend, you should use contractions and short, direct sentences. In informal invitations, use informal expressions like Hi Pete, Can you come?, Let me know if you can make it., etc.
"""

## 8 Read this invitation and answer the questions.
TEXT: An invitation
"""
Dear Mr Franklin,
On Saturday morning, a friend is arriving from the US. To celebrate this, my parents and I have decided to have a barbecue in our garden. We are inviting you to come to this barbecue. The barbecue starts at six o'clock in the evening. We are asking guests to bring drinks, but it is not necessary to bring food.
Please inform me if you can come.
Jonathan Smith
"""
? 1 Who makes the invitation? | Mr Franklin | Jonathan Smith* | Jonathan's friend from the US
? 2 Why do they make it? | A friend is arriving from the US.* | It's Jonathan's birthday. | They've got a new garden.
? 3 What is the invitation for? | a party at a restaurant | a barbecue* | a picnic in the park
? 4 Where should the person go? | to Jonathan's garden* | to the airport | to a café
? 5 What day/time should they go? | Saturday at six o'clock in the evening* | Saturday morning | Sunday at six o'clock
? 6 What should they bring? | food | drinks* | nothing
? 7 Is the invitation formal or informal? | formal* | informal
> 8 Why is it formal or informal? Give one example from the invitation.
